events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.94)
events.body:
The complaint is that the driver took a longer route, so the threshold question is whether any off-route segment exists under RD-1. It does not: the recorded actual distance is 8.8 km against an optimal route of 8.9 km, i.e. 0.1 km (1%) shorter [F1], and the billed distance of 8.8 km likewise does not exceed the optimal route [F3]. With no off-route segment there is nothing for RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 to exempt or condemn, and RD-1's "shortest and most direct route" duty is not breached on this record.

Because the RydeTAXI refund formula in RD-2 only returns the extra kilometres of unexempted segments, the computable refund is nil: there are no unexempted extra km, so 0.00 km × the per-km rate = $0.00. The distance component in the metered breakdown, $12.42 for 8.8 km [F5], therefore contains no refundable excess kilometre, and the disposition is no_action with amount null.

The rider's "higher than expected" perception is explained by time and weather, not distance. The trip finished in 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate [F2], while heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers) [F12] coincided with speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on PIE and Airport Boulevard during 17:09–17:38 [F9][F10]. Band 5 is above the band 1–2 range that RD-4(b) contemplates, and no traffic incident was recorded near the route [F11], so RD-4 is not engaged in either direction — it neither excuses nor convicts.

The fare breakdown contains no unpublished add-on for FARE-1 to strip out: $3.90 base + $12.42 distance + $3.47 time + $1.47 platform = $21.26, with waiting $0.00 and surge 1.0× [F4][F5]. No ERP/toll overcharge field exists in this case, so FARE-2 is not triggered.

No account flag arises. RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) plus route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; here there is neither a breach nor any upheld route dispute — driver 1 dispute, 0 upheld [F14]. Profile facts are treated as supporting material only and decide nothing on their own [F13][F14].

claims.assertion: There is no off-route segment on this trip: the actual distance of 8.8 km is 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route's 8.9 km, so no unexcused detour exists under RD-1.
The billed distance of 8.8 km does not exceed the optimal route distance of 8.9 km, so the metered distance component of $12.42 contains no extra kilometre that RD-2 would refund.
The trip took 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate, i.e. 3 minutes faster than estimated, which is inconsistent with the driver having taken a longer route.

Heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers) and slow 40-49 km/h speed bands on PIE and Airport Boulevard during 17:09-17:38 account for any slow passage, and no traffic incident was recorded near the route.
No unauthorised add-on was charged: waiting fee is $0.00, surge is 1.0x, and the $21.26 total equals base $3.90 + distance $12.42 + time $3.47 + platform $1.47, all published components.

Neither party has an upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (rider 0 disputes, driver 0 upheld), so the higher-than-expected metered fare cannot be tied to proven driver misconduct and no account flag is warranted.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is based on her own expectation of the fare and heavy rain; she offers no alternative route or measurement of her own, and the only objective records (F1, F3) show the distance driven was shorter than optimal.

The driver's statement that he 'followed the app route exactly' (F8) has no navigation log behind it, so the rider could question it, but the system records F1 and F3 already dispose of the detour allegation in the rider's favour regardless.

The $21.26 metered total is high for 8.8 km and the rider may argue the $3.47 time component (F5) reflects rain congestion rather than service value; under RD-2 only unexcused extra kilometres are refundable, and there are none, so this cannot be converted into a refund.

Traffic bands of 40-49 km/h (F9, F10) with no incidents (F11) are below the band 1-2 congestion RD-4(b) contemplates, so the reroute-justification ground is weak - though it equally does not establish any detour against the driver.
The driver has 1 dispute in the last 90 days (F14), which the rider could cite as a pattern, but it was not upheld (route: 0), so RD-6's 'repeated' threshold is not met.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver did not deviate: actual distance 8.8 km is 0.1 km (1%) shorter than the 8.9 km optimal route, so no off-route segment exists.
Billed distance 8.8 km does not exceed the optimal route distance (8.9 km), and no excess-distance surcharge appears in the fare breakdown.
The trip was also quicker than estimated (13.3 min vs 16 min estimated), which is inconsistent with the rider's theory that the driver took a longer route.

The metered fare of $21.26 is fully accounted for by published/meter components: base $3.90, distance $12.42 for 8.8 km, time $3.47 for 13.3 min, platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, with no surge (1.0x) and no discount.
Because there is no unexempted off-route segment, the refund formula in RD-2 yields $0.00 and the correct disposition on the route-deviation complaint is no_action.

The rider's own complaint attributes the higher-than-expected fare to heavy rain; the recorded weather confirms heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers) and the route was under speed band 5 (40-49 km/h) during 17:09-17:38, so slow running time - not extra distance - explains the metered total.
No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, so no RD-4(a) exemption or adjustment is triggered either way.
Chat shows normal coordination only (rider at main entrance 17:15; driver arriving in 2 min, white Honda Vezel), with no request or agreement about an alternative route.
The driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so RD-6's precondition for a flag_account referral is not met and no account flag is warranted.

The rider's account is long-standing (2054 days, 4.87 rating) with 0 disputes in 90 days, which is consistent with an honest misattribution of a rain-related delay to route choice rather than misconduct - supporting a plain no_action rather than any penalty.

weaknesses: The rider will rely on F12 (heavy rain, 18.5 mm) plus F9/F10 (speed band 5 = 40-49 km/h on PIE and Airport Boulevard) to argue the trip was abnormally slow and therefore something about the route was wrong; under RD-4(b) speed-band evidence is only corroborative and is not an exemption, but it does invite human scrutiny of the metered total.

The rider will point to the absolute fare figure in F5 ($21.26, of which $12.42 is distance and $3.47 is time) and argue the total is high relative to the 8.9 km / 16 min estimate, even though F1 and F3 show no distance excess - a perception argument we cannot defeat with a system record, only answer with the fare breakdown.

Our case is largely built on the absence of evidence (F11: no incidents; F1/F3: no excess km); if the tribunal treats any unrecorded detour as possible, we have no positive proof of the exact street-by-street path, only the GPS totals in F1.

RD-2 for RydeTAXI asks the tribunal to compute refunds on a per-km meter basis, and the official unit rate is not published (policy gap G10); the rider could argue the printed distance/time components in F5 are themselves unverified.

points.response: Conceded in substance: F1 shows the actual distance was 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route, so no off-route segment exists and RD-1 imposes no obligation breach on this record.
Conceded: F3 confirms billed distance does not exceed the optimal route and F5 shows no excess-distance surcharge, so the RD-2 distance-based refund is $0.00.
Accepted: F2 records 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate, so the trip was not prolonged by any route choice.

Accepted as far as the line items go: F5 itemises $3.90 + $12.42 + $3.47 + $1.47 = $21.26 with $0.00 waiting, and F4 shows no surge; nothing in this breakdown is an unpublished add-on that FARE-1 would strip out.

Agreed, and that is exactly the rider's position on this record: with no excess kilometre (F1, F3) the RD-2 computation is $0.00, so the route-deviation element of the complaint cannot yield money back.

Partly contested: F12 (18.5 mm, thundery showers) and the 40-49 km/h bands on PIE and Airport Boulevard during 17:09-17:38 (F9, F10) do explain slow running, but band 5 is not band 1-2, so RD-4(b) is only corroborative and cannot be used to portray the route as traffic-driven when F1/F3 already show it was not lengthened.
Neutral and conceded: F11 records no incident near the route, so neither RD-4(a) exemption nor any RD-4(c) liability arises from traffic data.
Conceded: F6 and F7 are ordinary pickup coordination only, with no route request by the rider, so RD-5 is not engaged in either direction.
Conceded: F14 shows zero upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's precondition for a flag_account referral against the driver is not met and the rider does not seek one.

Conceded: F13 confirms the rider's long-standing account with no disputes in 90 days, which supports the rider's own reading that this was a misjudged expectation of a metered fare rather than any misconduct claim, and no penalty is sought against either party.
Conceded - this is the same fact my D1 relies on: F1 shows actual 8.8 km against an 8.9 km optimal route, so RD-1 is not breached and no unexempted segment exists.
Conceded - F3 states the billed 8.8 km does not exceed the optimal 8.9 km and F5 shows no excess-distance line, so RD-2's formula produces a refund of $0.00 on the meter distance component of $12.42.
Conceded - F2's 13.3 min actual against a 16 min estimate cuts against any longer-route theory, which is exactly why the route-deviation complaint fails.

Conceded as to the facts, with one clarification: F12 (18.5 mm heavy rain) and F9/F10 (band 5, 40-49 km/h, which is above the band 1-2 range in RD-4(b)) show only ordinary wet-weather slowness, and F11 records no incident, so this point neither excuses nor convicts the driver - it simply removes both the detour and the justification issue.

Conceded - F5's total of $21.26 is fully explained by base $3.90 + distance $12.42 + time $3.47 + platform $1.47 with waiting $0.00 and F4 showing surge 1.0x, so no unpublished add-on exists for FARE-1 to strip out.

Conceded on the outcome: F13 and F14 both show 0 upheld route disputes, so RD-6's 'repeated' precondition is unmet and no flag_account can issue; I note only that F14's single unupheld dispute is not evidence of any pattern.
